posts:
Gunfire in the early hours shatters the peace of a Dublin neighborhood. Gardaí cordon off a house on Pearse Street after a firearm is discharged.
Evidence: Public safety, Active gunfire, Police response
#Aletheia #Dublin

Gardaí reported they are investigating a firearm discharge near Macken Street in Dublin 2. No injuries have been reported, and enquiries are ongoing.
Stated Judgement: (0.00, 0.00) — Neutral

The discharge of a firearm in a dense residential area represents a severe threat to public safety, regardless of whether anyone was physically struck by the bullets.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.85, -0.85) — Greater Evil

In the early hours of the morning, a firearm was discharged near the junction of Macken Street and Pearse Street, leading to a police cordon and ongoing forensic enquiries.

The Bright Side:
No injuries were reported from the incident, preventing a potential tragedy in a busy urban residential area.
The Plane Error is focusing only on the lack of physical injuries (WHAT) instead of the severe threat posed by the presence of active shooters in the community (WHO).

The perpetrator executed a highly destructive act, introducing extreme strain into the community. This represents a complete failure of empathy, projecting violence onto a residential space and forcing a defensive institutional response.

When you map the gap between stated safety and the reality of gunfire, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Evil. Reckless violence destabilizes local communities.

The Unavoidable Lie: The area is perfectly secure just because no one was injured this time.

GARDAÍ ARE INVESTIGATING following a report that a firearm was discharged on Pearse Street, Dublin 2, in the early hours of this morning.

A garda spokesperson confirmed that no injuries were reported at the time.

A house near the junction between Macken Street and Pearse Street was cordoned off and gardaí were at the scene this morning.

A section of the footpath in front of the house was also cordoned off, causing pedestrians to walk on to the road to get past.

Garda enquiries are ongoing.
